author: blu
body: The on-disk layout it reads -- the sector size, the entry-header offsets, the superblock fields -- is Foreword chapter FactLog, the one definition DiskFacts shares; the kind-30 record inside an entry is decoded by Foreword chapter SourceDefWire, likewise shared with the writer. What is left here is the part that is genuinely this reader's: the effectful walk over the sectors, and the assembly of the results into a bundle.

author: blu
body: Two candidate superblocks, and the reader trusts the one with the higher generation whose magic is intact. A sector with the wrong magic reports a generation below any real one, so it never wins; if neither is a superblock the log is empty and the walk covers nothing. Both generations and both log heads are read up front so the choice itself is pure.

author: blu
body: The kind-30 record's wire format -- the ninth-pipe rule, the length-prefixed content, the signature's hex -- is decoded by Foreword chapter SourceDefWire, the one place that also encodes it on the way in. A line that is not in that format (an old pointer-shaped record with no ninth pipe) decodes to None and is skipped; there is nothing to offer.

author: blu
body: The work becomes the Fact its own hash addresses -- sdw-hash over sdw-content, the digest a quotation names -- wearing the timestamp and author the signature covers, not the entry header's timestamp. An unsigned record is offered; a signed one is published, so the gate answers ImportUnsigned and ImportForged where each is the truth.

author: blu
body: Everything the disk holds, added to the bundle already in hand. The compiler passes the bundle it built from the offered-works blob, so the store supplements the blob rather than replacing it: a quotation the blob satisfies still resolves, and one it does not is looked for on the disk.
